paragraphs: Children in care in Essex are looked after by Essex County Council's own fostering service and by the independent agencies listed on this page. The council's fostering team is rated Outstanding by Ofsted. Essex is also one of 11 councils in Foster East, a partnership across the East of England, where more than 7,000 children are in care at any one time. The partnership's aim is to help children stay in their own community, close to friends and family and at their usual school.

The council says almost anyone can foster, whether they are retired, working or have a family of their own, and that fostering ranges from one weekend a month to full-time care, so there is room for different lifestyles. It also welcomes approved carers who want to transfer from another fostering service.

Essex gives an example of what carers receive: on average £537.12 a week for looking after one child aged 11 to 15, which it says comes to £27,930.24 a year, most of it tax-free. There are extra payments for birthdays, Christmas and summer days out, and expenses are refunded for travel to training and family visits and for specialist equipment.

Each carer agrees a learning plan with their social worker, with some courses such as first aid required and others chosen to suit the kind of fostering they do. Social workers visit in person, there are monthly local support groups, and an emergency line is open around the clock.
If you live in Essex, it is worth speaking to the council and to two or three of the agencies below, and comparing their training, support and pay before you decide.

sources.title: Why foster with Essex? (Essex County Council)
